{"prompt": "def _compute_cell_circumcenters(self):\n        \"\"\"Computes the center of the circumsphere of each cell.\n        \"\"\"", "output": "\n        import numpy as np\n        from scipy.spatial import Delaunay\n\n        points = self.points\n        tri = Delaunay(points)\n        cells = tri.simplices\n\n        # For each cell, we need the 4 vertices of the tetrahedron\n        pts = points[cells] # Shape: (num_cells, 4, dim)\n\n        # Relative coordinates of 3 vertices with respect to the first\n        a = pts[:, 0, :]\n        b = pts[:, 1, :] - a\n        c = pts[:, 2, :] - a\n        d = pts[:, 3, :] - a\n\n        # Using the formula for the circumcenter of a tetrahedron\n        # b_sq = |b|^2, c_sq = |c|^2, d_sq = |d|^2\n        b_sq = np.sum(b**2, axis=1)\n        c_sq = np.sum(c**2, axis=1)\n        d_sq = np.sum(d**2, axis=1)\n\n        # Determinant of the matrix [b, c, d]\n        det = 2 * np.linalg.det(np.stack([b, c, d], axis=-1))\n\n        # Cross products for the numerator\n        # (b_sq * (c x d) + c_sq * (d x b) + d_sq * (b x c)) / det\n        cross_cd = np.cross(c, d)\n        cross_db = np.cross(d, b)\n        cross_bc = np.cross(b, c)\n\n        num = (b_sq[:, None] * cross_cd +\n               c_sq[:, None] * cross_db +\n               d_sq[:, None] * cross_bc)\n\n        circumcenters = a + num / det[:, None]\n        return circumcenters\n", "solution": "\n        # {"prompt": "def rcs(J,P,R,T,p,c,a,RUB):\n    \"\"\"rcs -- model for the resource constrained scheduling problem\n    Parameters:\n        - J: set of jobs\n        - P: set of precedence constraints between jobs\n        - R: set of resources\n        - T: number of periods\n        - p[j]: processing time of job j\n        - c[j,t]: cost incurred when job j starts processing on period t.\n        - a[j,r,t]: resource r usage for job j on period t (after job starts)\n        - RUB[r,t]: upper bound for resource r on period t\n    Returns a model, ready to be solved.\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n    from pulp import LpProblem, LpVariable, lpSum, LpMinimize\n\n    model = LpProblem(\"RCSP\", LpMinimize)\n\n    # x[j, t] = 1 if job j starts at time t\n    x = LpVariable.dicts(\"x\", [(j, t) for j in J for t in range(T)], cat=\"Binary\")\n\n    # Objective: Minimize total cost\n    model += lpSum(c[j, t] * x[j, t] for j in J for t in range(T))\n\n    # Constraint 1: Each job must start exactly once\n    for j in J:\n        model += lpSum(x[j, t] for t in range(T)) == 1\n\n    # Constraint 2: Precedence constraints (j, k) in P means j must finish before k starts\n    for (j, k) in P:\n        model += lpSum(t * x[j, t] for t in range(T)) + p[j] <= lpSum(t * x[k, t] for t in range(T))\n\n    # Constraint 3: Resource constraints for each resource r at each time t\n    for r in R:\n        for t in range(T):\n            # Job j uses resource r at time t if it started at time s such that s <= t < s + p[j]\n            # The resource usage is a[j, r, t-s] where t-s is the relative time since start\n            model += lpSum(x[j, s] * a[j, r, t - If None the distance is set to\n       1/sqrt(n) where n is the number of nodes. {"prompt": "def iteration(self, node_status=True):\n        \"\"\"\n        Execute a single model iteration\n\n        :return: Iteration_id, Incremental node status (dictionary node->status)\n        \"\"\"", "output": "\n        iteration_id = self.current_iteration\n        self.current_iteration += 1\n\n        incremental_status = {}\n        for node in self.nodes:\n            if node_status:\n                status = self.compute_node_status(node)\n                incremental_status[node] = status\n\n        self.update_model_state(incremental_status)\n\n        return iteration_id, incremental_status\n", "solution": "\n        # One iteration changes the opinion of N agent pairs using the following procedure:\n        # - first one agent is selected\n        # - then a second agent is selected based on a probability that decreases with the distance to the first agent\n        # - if the two agents have a distance smaller than epsilon, then they change their status to the average of\n        # their previous statuses\n\n        self.clean_initial_status(None)\n\n        actual_status = {node: nstatus for node, nstatus in future.utils.iteritems(self.status)}\n\n        if self.actual_iteration == 0:\n            self.actual_iteration += 1\n            delta, node_count, status_delta = self.status_delta(self.status)\n            if node_status:\n                return {\"iteration\": 0, \"status\": self.status.copy(),\n                        \"node_count\": node_count.copy(), \"status_delta\": status_delta.copy()}\n            else:\n                return {\"iteration\": 0, \"status\": {},\n                        \"node_count\": node_count.copy(), \"status_delta\": status_delta.copy()}\n\n        # interact with peers\n        for i in range(0, self.graph.number_of_nodes()):\n            # select a random node\n            n1 = list(self.graph.nodes())[np.random.randint(0, self.graph.number_of_nodes())]\n            # select all of the node's neighbours (no digraph possible)\n            neighbours = list(self.graph.neighbors(n1))\n            if len(neighbours) == 0:\n                continue\n        \n            # Due to sampling problems, the measured\n    deformation is overestimated and must be corrected.\n\n    The correction formula is described in :cite:`Herold2017`.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    area_um: float or ndarray\n        Apparent (2D image) area in µm² of the event(s)\n    px_um: float\n        The detector pixel size in µm.\n    inplace: bool\n        Change the deformation values in-place\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    deform_delta: float or ndarray\n        Error of the deformation of the event(s) that must be\n        subtracted from `deform`.\n        deform_corr = deform -  deform_delta\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n    import numpy as np\n    return (np.pi * px_um**2) / (4 * area_um)\n", "solution": "\n    # A triple-exponential decay can be used to correct for pixelation\n    # for apparent cell areas between 10 and 1250µm².\n    # For 99 different radii between 0.4 μm and 20 μm circular objects were\n    # simulated on a pixel grid with the pixel resolution of 340 nm/pix.
